key_insight: Adults with weaker preoperative social connection had worse postoperative outcomes in several analyses, especially higher early mortality and non-home discharge, while the primary survival result was not statistically definitive.
clinical_relevance: Social connection may function as a prognostic marker before surgery, suggesting value for identifying patients who may need extra perioperative support and discharge planning.
method: Systematic review and meta-analysis of adults undergoing surgery
33,301 records screened; 454 reports from 445 studies included
Random-effects REML models with modified Hartung-Knapp intervals; certainty rated with GRADE
evidence_signal: The strongest signals were for early postoperative mortality (OR 1.50, 95% CI 1.12-2.01) and non-home discharge (OR 1.95, 95% CI 1.35-2.81), while postoperative survival had a CI crossing 1 (HR 1.37, 95% CI 0.99-1.89).
watch_item: Most evidence came from observational studies and largely from marital status, so social connection measures were heterogeneous and causality cannot be assumed.
paper_title: Preoperative Social Connection and Postoperative Outcomes in Adults Undergoing Surgery: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
